title: What's the plan for the MacArthur Center site, and how settled is it?
summary: What the City has said and done about the former MacArthur Center mall at 300 Monticello Avenue. The City owns the site (bought in 2023), hired HG80 as master developer (2025), closed the mall on June 27, 2026, and describes a mixed-use district of market-rate housing, hotel rooms, street-level retail and restored streets, opening in 2030 by its own timeline. The adopted FY2027 capital plan lists $72 million over five years; its FY2027 and FY2028 money is for demolition and infrastructure. What isn't settled: as of July 2026 the development agreement with Hg80 was still being negotiated, demolition had moved to late 2027 or early 2028, and the housing form and a grocery tenant were not final. City Council approves the agreements, and state law requires a public hearing before the City disposes of the land. Siren's legislation index (Council meetings through October 22, 2026) holds no ordinance approving an agreement with Hg80.

what_would_help.text: Watch City Council agendas for the design and development agreement with Hg80: it is the decision that sets what gets built and when.
A sale or lease of the site to a developer needs a public hearing first; that hearing is the formal chance to speak on the terms.

pending: A third-party recap (NorfolkTV via Govly) of Council's September 29, 2026 work session says staff were drafting a purchase and development agreement for Council in November or December; not yet confirmed in Council's own records.

The 2025 studies on the City's MacArthur Center page (redevelopment feasibility, due diligence, market study, retail research, apartment feasibility appraisal, grocery study) are not yet read for findings.
Reported 2023 purchase prices differ (WHRO in June 2023: $11 million; the City's appropriation: $18,000,000 to acquire and operate). Only the appropriation is a finding.
The FY2026 budget cut $3,988,000 of mall operating expenses "that the consultant is paying currently"; who the consultant is and why it pays them isn't clear from the budget book.
